body.statement:
For every positive \(N,T,n_1,\ldots,n_S\), every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and \(P\)-almost every admissible event state,
\[
P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
For fixed sample sizes, call an interval \(I\) finite-sample conditionally honest if it is observed-data measurable and satisfies this same inequality with \(I\) in place of \(C_\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), there are constants \(0<c_\alpha<C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) such that
\[
c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}
\le
\inf_{I:\,\text{finite-sample conditionally honest}}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\]
The lower bound also holds for uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest interval sequences by an \(\epsilon\)-slack argument.  Coverage conditions on the complete historical design, \(E_0\), and all donors; treats each unit's history as one bounded cluster; uses the exact Taylor allowance and full-sample donor fourth-moment calibration; and combines the three failure probabilities by Bonferroni.  The result requires neither temporal outcome mixing within a unit, identical unit response laws, studentization, a dense-local-site condition, nor sequential overlap.  The log-adjusted spacing term is uniform and unavoidable under design-only geometric beta mixing and the maintained marginal-density assumptions.
body.justification: The full-data interval has exact finite-sample conditional coverage and asymptotically matches the four-channel expected-length lower bound.
body.gap: Coverage needs no selector-tail argument, donor splitting, studentization, identical unit response law, response-variance premise, or temporal-outcome restriction.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain finite-sample conditionally honest inference at every relative-growth configuration.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On each successful fit, polynomial reproduction (12) applied to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\), followed by (13), gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{62}
\]
After cohort weighting, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the historical unit-cluster variables
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_t a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} gives \(\mathbb E[U_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]=0\): donor independence permits the donors to be added to the conditioning field.  Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the variables independent over \((s,i)\) under that conditioning.  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|.
\]
If a conditionally centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its conditional exponential moment by the endpoint mixture having the same mean.  Twice differentiating the logarithm of this mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{63}
\]
Multiplication of (63) over the independent unit clusters, Chernoff's inequality, optimization over \(v>0\), and repetition for \(-U\) yield
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s,i}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{64}
\]
This uses no mixing or independence along the calendar within a unit.

Similarly define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(V_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\), donor independence preserves that centering after adding the donors, and cross-unit independence makes the variables conditionally independent.  Their range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same argument gives
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s,i}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{65}
\]
The two events in (64)--(65) are combined by a union bound, so no independence between a unit's historical path and event outcome is needed.

For donor calibration put \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\) and \(W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_jY_j\).  Conditional iid donor replication gives \(\mathbb E[Y_j\mid E_0]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding the fourth power and grouping the all-equal and three paired index patterns gives exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{66}
\]
Define the donor-deviation event
\[
\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}.
\]
Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{67}
\]
Coordinatewise projection onto \([0,1]^{Sd}\) cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), which lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds consequently give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_N/\sqrt N
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{68}
\]
On the observable good event, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\), so the upper half of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (68) imply
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{69}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) denote the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j))\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\).  Each potential-outcome contrast lies in \([-B,B]\), and the cohort weights are positive and sum to one, so \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) deterministically.  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), the identification equality, (62), and (69) decompose the estimator error into the event fluctuation, the historical fluctuation, and two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Hence noncoverage implies failure of (64) or (65).  Iterated conditioning gives the finite-sample bound
\[
\begin{aligned}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{70}
\]
No selector tail bound is used for (70).  Thus coverage is exact for every positive sample size and every law in the enlarged subclass.

For expected length, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives deterministically on a successful fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{71}
\]
The kernel support and the same deterministic weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
Applying the selector moment with exponent \(\lambda\), and using Cauchy--Schwarz across the fixed cohorts, gives
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{72}
\]
Since \(D\) and \(\alpha\) are fixed, (66) makes \(q_N\le C\), whence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{73}
\]
The selector lemma gives \(P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the stated arrays.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), and eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Since \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on \(\mathcal G\), (71)--(73) prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{74}
\]

For the lower bound, reduce the fixed perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so every channel affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for a fixed \(a_0>0\); for the rare-block pair reduce its fixed active-block intensity.  Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest, let \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) be a channel pair's target values, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\).  Uniform honesty and domination by the two laws imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{75}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Therefore
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{76}
\]
Maximizing (76) over the four channels gives \(c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  If a sequence is only uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest, then for every \(\epsilon>0\) its two noncoverage probabilities are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Choosing \(\epsilon<a_0/4\) replaces the final lower bound in (75) by \(a_0-2\epsilon\ge a_0/2\), proving the same rate.  Combining (70), (74), and (76) proves all claims.
